objectives: Provide respectful, nonjudgmental triage for post-miscarriage complications.
Identify signs of post-abortion sepsis and initiate urgent referral-level management.
Document confidentiality, emergency interventions, and referral counseling clearly.
takeaways: Fever, hypotension, and foul-smelling discharge after pregnancy loss suggest sepsis risk.
Compassionate language and privacy are part of clinical safety, not optional extras.
Do not delay stabilization and referral while seeking complete outpatient diagnostics.
learnCaseOverrides.blurb: A woman presents with fever and abdominal pain after miscarriage and fears being judged. Choose care that is both clinically urgent and respectful.

sections.title: Chief complaint
sections.text: Fever, lower abdominal pain, and foul vaginal discharge two days after miscarriage

sections.title: Patient concern
sections.text: She speaks quietly and asks if staff will blame her for what happened.

coach.title: Lydia arrives anxious and unwell
coach.body: She is shivering and visibly distressed. Your approach must combine emergency care with privacy and dignity.
coach.quote: “Please help me... I was afraid to come because people may judge me.”

teach.label: Clinical framing
teach.text: Respectful communication improves disclosure and speed of care in obstetric emergencies.

critical.title: Sepsis danger pattern
critical.body: Fever + hypotension + tachycardia after miscarriage indicates urgent risk.

coach.title: Choose the safest opening action
coach.body: Pick the option that addresses both immediate physiology and patient dignity.

options.text: Move to a private space, start sepsis triage, and begin urgent stabilization/referral planning
Question her about the miscarriage details in front of the waiting line before treating
Give oral pain medicines and ask her to return if fever persists tomorrow
Delay emergency care until legal documentation is completed

question.right: Correct. BP 90/58, HR 124, and temperature 39.1 C indicate urgent sepsis risk. Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023 supports immediate stabilization and referral; respectful privacy improves safe care.
question.wrong: This chart shows hemodynamic instability after miscarriage. Delaying care for interrogation or routine workflow is unsafe and undermines trust.

coach.title: What should be done before transfer?
coach.body: Her blood pressure is dropping and she remains febrile.

question.prompt: Which management choice is best now?

options.text: Start IV fluids, give empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics per protocol, and arrange urgent referral
Wait for all lab results before initiating treatment
Treat as uncomplicated malaria because she has fever
Provide only oral antibiotics and routine follow-up in 72 hours

question.right: Correct. Persistent hypotension (88/56) with post-miscarriage infection signs requires immediate sepsis-oriented care and urgent referral, not delayed outpatient management.
question.wrong: This patient is unstable. Delaying emergency treatment for full workup or malaria-first assumptions can be life-threatening.

rows.label: Observed
rows.value: Fever 39.1 C, BP 88/56, foul discharge, pelvic pain

rows.label: Given
rows.value: IV fluids + empiric antibiotics + urgent transfer arranged

rows.label: Counseling
rows.value: Explained emergency risk and reassured nonjudgmental care

coach.title: What is essential in counseling and handover?
coach.body: Choose the response that preserves safety and dignity.

question.prompt: How should you complete this transfer?

options.text: Use nonjudgmental language, explain emergency need, and send a full referral note with interventions
Tell her she caused the illness and must confess details before referral
Send without documentation to avoid difficult conversations
Reassure only and keep her overnight at HC III for observation

question.right: Correct. Compassionate counseling improves consent and adherence, while complete handover communicates her instability and treatment already started.
question.wrong: Judgmental or incomplete communication harms care. This case requires both urgent transfer and trauma-informed respectful practice.

sections.title: Case outcome
sections.text: You identified post-miscarriage sepsis risk, stabilized early, and referred urgently with respectful care.
sections.emphasis: Nonjudgmental communication and emergency action were both essential.

coach.title: Key teaching points
coach.body: Lydia's fever, hypotension, tachycardia, and foul discharge after pregnancy loss indicate high-risk infection requiring immediate referral-level care. Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023 supports urgent stabilization and transfer, while respectful communication protects disclosure and timely treatment.

teach.label: Clinician review
teach.text: In post-miscarriage emergencies, dignity is part of clinical quality: privacy, nonjudgment, and rapid treatment should happen together.
